speaker: CHRIS
text: That's not... we didn't... Carl. Look outside.

speaker: TRUCKER
text: Hey! You the guys who said ice cream causes crime?!

speaker: CHRIS
text: Drive. Drive now.

speaker: CHRIS
text: I think we lost them. And the ice cream union's goodwill.

speaker: CHRIS
text: Four links. A cause, a common cause, a coincidence and a shrug. That's a good night's science.

speaker: CHRIS
text: Next time we say 'common cause' slower. And louder. Near fewer ice cream vans.

speaker: CJ
text: Man, that radio guy's gonna be talking about weather control for a year.

speaker: CHRIS
text: Probably. But a few thousand people heard the difference between a cause and a coincidence tonight. That's not nothing.

speaker: NEWS
text: Radio Free Fierro drew record ratings last night with an unusually calm debate about ice cream.

speaker: NEWS
text: Ice cream vans protested outside a Doherty laboratory last night over remarks on pirate radio. No ice cream was harmed.

speaker: CHRIS
text: Carl. Tomorrow we open the doors. Everything, in public. Ready?

speaker: CJ
text: Ready for what?

speaker: CHRIS
text: The open experiment.

speaker: CHRIS
text: Tomorrow we run the plate experiment in public. Everything open: the method, the data, the mistakes.

speaker: CHRIS
text: And three independent groups run the same experiment at the same time, across town. If they get our result, it's real.

speaker: CJ
text: And if they don't?

speaker: CHRIS
text: Then we were wrong in front of everybody, and we learn something. Win-win.

speaker: BRACKET
text: Gentlemen! Lyle Bracket, Ovid Venture Partners. The door was open. I love an open door.

speaker: BRACKET
text: Two hundred and fifty thousand dollars for an exclusive licence on R.A.I.N. We close the code, we polish the brand, everybody gets rich.

speaker: CHRIS
text: That's generous. And no.

speaker: BRACKET
text: Closed systems sell, Mister Woodyard. Open ones get copied. The offer stands. For your friend, too.

speaker: CJ
text: He seems nice.

speaker: CHRIS
text: He seems like a man who's never been told no by a garage. Let's get the kits out.

speaker: CHRIS
text: Three replication kits: a plate, a generator, a pinch of sand, and instructions a teenager can follow.

speaker: CHRIS
text: One to the physics teacher at Garcia High, one to the ham radio club in Ocean Flats, one to the kid who won the science fair.

speaker: TEACHER
text: Real equipment? For my class? Oh, they are going to lose their minds.

speaker: CJ
text: Four forty-two hertz, tomorrow at noon. Write down whatever you see.

speaker: TEACHER
text: Even if it's nothing?

speaker: CJ
text: Especially if it's nothing. That's what he says.

speaker: HAM
text: A Chladni plate. We'll calibrate the generator against our frequency standard. To the hertz.

speaker: CJ
text: Man, you're gonna be good at this.

speaker: KID
text: If your result doesn't replicate, I'm putting that in my report.

speaker: CJ
text: Kid, that's exactly what he wants.

speaker: CHRIS
text: Black sedan, three cars back. It's been there since Garcia.

speaker: CHRIS
text: Ovid's people. If they rattle the van hard enough, the kits crack. Lose them.

speaker: CHRIS
text: That knock broke a kit. One group fewer.

speaker: CHRIS
text: They've dropped off. Good driving.

speaker: CHRIS
text: The pier. Look at all these people. Some of them even came on purpose.

speaker: OFFICIAL
text: Deputy Commissioner Halvorsen, procurement. This event has no permit for experimental equipment. Shut it down.

speaker: CHRIS
text: It's a speaker and a metal plate, Commissioner. The schematics are on the registry. You're welcome to check them.

speaker: OFFICIAL
text: I am not here to check things. I am here to stop things.

speaker: CJ
text: Lady, that's the whole problem with this city.

speaker: CHRIS
text: The generator's dead. Somebody pulled the fuse. There! The guy in the overalls!

speaker: CHRIS
text: Carl, get that fuse back. Don't hurt him.

speaker: CJ
text: Give it here, man! Now!

speaker: CHRIS
text: Fuse is in. We're live.

speaker: CHRIS
text: He got away. We'll run it off the van battery. It'll be quieter, but it'll work.

speaker: CHRIS
text: Four hundred and forty-two hertz. Watch the sand.

speaker: CROWD
text: Whoa! It's making a pattern!

speaker: TEACHER
text: Garcia High here! Same pattern! Crosses and curves, exactly like your picture!

speaker: HAM
text: Ocean Flats Amateur Radio Club. Mode confirmed at four forty-two, plus or minus one.

speaker: KID
text: It worked. I hate that it worked. It's in my report.

speaker: CHRIS
text: R.A.I.N.'s question for all of us: does the result hold up?

speaker: CHRIS
text: Accepted. Independent groups, independent equipment, same result. That's what real looks like.

speaker: CHRIS
text: Reject it? Carl, they all got the pattern. On their own kit.

speaker: CHRIS
text: We don't need to abstain. More than one independent replication. We can say it.

speaker: CHRIS
text: Abstained. One replication is a promising start, not a confirmation. We publish it as exactly that.

speaker: CHRIS
text: Accept, on one replication? I'd love to. That's exactly why we shouldn't.

speaker: CHRIS
text: Reject? One group confirmed it. That's not nothing. It's not enough, either.

speaker: OFFICIAL
text: ...The city will be reviewing its permit process.

speaker: BRACKET
text: Carl. A word. Your friend won't sell. But friends can be persuaded.

speaker: BRACKET
text: Fifty thousand dollars. Cash. All you have to do is talk him round.

speaker: CJ
text: ...Fifty thousand?

speaker: BRACKET
text: Pleasure doing business. Do your best with him. Or don't. I'll know.

speaker: CJ
text: He already told you no. That's the only answer you're getting from either of us.

speaker: BRACKET
text: Shame. Open systems get copied, you know.

speaker: CJ
text: Yeah. That's the point, genius.

speaker: NEWS
text: An independent San Fierro lab demonstrated a sound experiment live at the pier, while schools and a radio club across the city reproduced it at the same time.

speaker: NEWS
text: The lab's code and data are freely available on an open registry. A venture firm's offer to license the work was declined.

speaker: CHRIS
text: Forty thousand downloads. Three replications. Two of them by people under eighteen.

speaker: CJ
text: So what now? More experiments?

speaker: CHRIS
text: Always. The lab's open whenever you want it, Carl. R.A.I.N. has questions nobody's asked yet.

speaker: CJ
text: Long as none of them gets the cops on me.

speaker: CHRIS
text: I can't promise that. But I can promise we'll check the evidence first.
